outcomes.text: Explain the difference between book-keeping and accounting.
State why businesses measure profit and loss.
Explain how accounting information helps monitor progress and make decisions.
Explain what assets, liabilities and owner's equity mean.
Explain and apply the accounting equation.

topics.title: 2.1 The double entry system of book-keeping

outcomes.text: Outline how double entry book-keeping works.
Process accounting data using double entry.
Prepare ledger accounts.
Post transactions to ledger accounts.
Balance ledger accounts and transfer balances to financial statements.
Interpret ledger accounts and their balances.
Recognise the split into sales ledger, purchases ledger and nominal (general) ledger.
Recognise and understand invoice, debit note, credit note, statement of account, cheque and receipt.
Complete pro-forma business documents.
Use invoices, credit notes, cheque counterfoils, paying-in slips, receipts and bank statements as sources of information.
Explain the advantages of using books of prime entry.
Process data in the cash book, petty cash book, sales and purchases journals, returns journals and the general journal.
Post ledger entries from the books of prime entry.
Distinguish and account for trade discount and cash discounts.
Explain the cash book's dual role as book of prime entry and ledger account.
Record bank transfers and other electronic payments and receipts.
Explain and apply the imprest system of petty cash.
Understand that a trial balance lists ledger balances at a date.
Outline the uses and limitations of a trial balance.
Prepare a trial balance from balances and amend one containing errors.

subtopics.title: Errors not shown by the trial balance

outcomes.text: Explain errors of commission, compensating, complete reversal, omission, original entry and principle.
Correct errors with journal entries.
Explain the suspense account as a temporary balancing measure.
Correct errors through suspense accounts.
Adjust profit or loss after correcting errors.
Understand the effect of corrections on the statement of financial position.
Understand the use and purpose of a bank statement.
Update the cash book for charges, interest, errors, credit transfers, direct debits, dividends and standing orders.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement including bank errors, uncredited deposits and unpresented cheques.
Understand the purposes of purchases and sales ledger control accounts.
Identify books of prime entry as the sources of control account entries.
Prepare control accounts with credit transactions, receipts, discounts, returns, irrecoverable debts, dishonoured cheques, interest, contras, refunds and opening and closing balances.

topics.title: 4.1 Capital and revenue expenditure and receipts

outcomes.text: Distinguish and account for capital and revenue expenditure.
Distinguish and account for capital and revenue receipts.
Calculate and comment on the effect of wrong treatment on profit.
Calculate and comment on the effect on asset valuations.

topics.title: 4.2 Accounting for depreciation and disposal of non-current assets

outcomes.text: Define depreciation and explain why it is accounted for.
Describe the straight-line, reducing balance and revaluation methods.
Prepare ledger accounts and journals for the provision for depreciation.
Prepare ledger accounts and journals for sale of non-current assets, including disposal accounts.
Recognise the importance of matching costs and revenues.
Record accrued and prepaid expenses in ledgers and journals.
Record accrued and prepaid income in ledgers and journals.

topics.title: 4.4 Irrecoverable debts and provision for doubtful debts

outcomes.text: Understand irrecoverable debts and recovery of debts written off.
Record irrecoverable debts.
Record recovery of debts written off.
Explain why a provision for doubtful debts is kept.
Record the creation of, and changes to, the provision.
Understand valuation at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
Prepare simple inventory valuation statements.
Explain how a wrong inventory valuation affects gross profit, profit, equity and assets.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of being a sole trader.
Explain why income statements and statements of financial position are prepared.
Explain the difference between trading and service businesses.
Prepare income statements for trading and service businesses.
Understand that the statement of financial position records assets and liabilities at a date.
Recognise and define non-current, intangible and current assets, current and non-current liabilities and capital.
Understand how items in the statement relate to each other.
Prepare statements of financial position for trading and service businesses.
Adjust for depreciation by straight-line, reducing balance and revaluation.
Adjust for accrued and prepaid expenses and income.
Adjust for irrecoverable debts and provisions for doubtful debts.
Adjust for goods taken by the owner for own use.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of forming a partnership.
Outline the importance and contents of a partnership agreement.
Explain the purpose of an appropriation account.
Prepare income statements, appropriation accounts and statements of financial position.
Record interest on loans, capital and drawings, partners' salaries and the split of profit or loss.
Make the year-end adjustments from sole trader accounts.
Explain the uses of and differences between capital and current accounts.
Draw up partners' capital and current accounts as ledgers and within the statement of financial position.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of a limited company.
Understand limited liability and equity.
Understand the capital structure: preference shares, ordinary shares, general reserve and retained earnings.
Distinguish issued, called-up and paid-up share capital.
Distinguish share capital from loan capital (debentures).
Prepare income statements, statements of changes in equity and statements of financial position.
Make the year-end adjustments from sole trader accounts.
Distinguish receipts and payments accounts from income and expenditure accounts.
Prepare receipts and payments accounts.
Prepare accounts for revenue-generating activities such as refreshments and subscriptions.
Prepare income and expenditure accounts and statements of financial position.
Make the year-end adjustments from sole trader accounts.
Define and calculate the accumulated fund.
Distinguish direct from indirect costs.
Understand direct material, direct labour, prime cost and factory overheads.
Understand and adjust for work in progress.
Calculate factory cost of production.
Prepare manufacturing accounts, income statements and statements of financial position.
Make the year-end adjustments from sole trader accounts.
Explain the disadvantages of not keeping a full set of records.
Prepare opening and closing statements of affairs.
Calculate profit or loss from changes in capital.
Calculate sales, purchases, gross profit, receivables, payables and other figures from incomplete information.
Apply mark-up, margin and inventory turnover to find missing figures.
Prepare income statements and statements of financial position from incomplete records.
Make the year-end adjustments from sole trader accounts.

topics.title: 6.1 Calculation and understanding of accounting ratios

outcomes.text: Understand, calculate and explain gross margin.
Understand, calculate and explain profit margin.
Understand, calculate and explain return on capital employed (ROCE).
Understand, calculate and explain the current ratio.
Understand, calculate and explain the liquid (acid test) ratio.
Understand, calculate and explain the rate of inventory turnover.
Understand, calculate and explain trade receivables turnover in days.
Understand, calculate and explain trade payables turnover in days.
Prepare and comment on statements comparing results for different years.
Recommend ways to improve profitability and working capital.
Explain what the gap between gross margin and profit margin says about efficiency.
Explain how gross profit and profit relate to inventory valuation, inventory turnover, revenue, expenses and equity.
Understand the problems of comparing firms.
Apply accounting ratios to compare firms.
Explain how owners and managers use accounting information.
Explain how trade payables and banks use accounting information.
Explain how investors, club members and other parties such as governments and tax authorities use accounting information.
Recognise limits due to historic cost.
Recognise limits due to difficulties of definition.
Recognise limits due to non-financial aspects.
Explain and recognise matching, business entity, consistency and duality.
Explain and recognise going concern, historic cost and materiality.
Explain and recognise money measurement, prudence and realisation.
Recognise the influence of international accounting standards.
Understand the aims of comparability, relevance, reliability and understandability in choosing policies.
